terms.grammar: adverb; at the head of its clause or after the word it stresses
evidence: Cic. Att. 12.41.1: scīre tamen volēbam ubi essēs
terms.comment: The “however” that answers a concession, said or understood (etsī, quamquam, quamvīs, cum): “even so”.

terms.gloss: however, but, on the other hand
terms.grammar: conjunction; never first in its clause, but after its first word or phrase
evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.18.2: maximē autem date operam ut valeātis
terms.comment: A light “but” that sets one thing beside another, not “nevertheless”; where nothing is set against it, leave it out.

evidence: Cic. Att. 6.2.2: est magnum illud quidem vērum tamen multiplex puerī ingenium
Cic. Off. 1.51: nihilō minus ipsī lūcet
Cato Agr. 39.2: nihilō minus sūmptum futūrum

phrases.latin: nihil erat quod scrīberem. scīre tamen volēbam ubi essēs
phrases.english: I had nothing to write; however, I wanted to know where you were

phrases.latin: etiam Hirtiō cēnam dedī, sine pāvōne tamen
phrases.english: I even gave Hirtius dinner, without a peacock, however

phrases.latin: nātūram expellēs furcā, tamen ūsque recurret
phrases.english: drive nature out with a pitchfork, and she will keep coming back all the same

sources: Lewis & Short: tamen · Lewis & Short: autem · Lewis & Short: verumtamen · Lewis & Short: nihil (nihilominus)
